newsitem.title: INDIA: A year of political upheaval in India.
newsitem.headline: A year of political upheaval in India.

text.p: NEW DELHI, April 21 - Following is a chronology of major political developments in India since the centre-left United Front alliance took power last June after general elections.
June 1, 1996 - Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, leader of 13-party United Front coalition, is sworn in.
June 5 - Deve Gowda's government unveils policies signalling continued economic reforms, a tough line on nuclear issues and conciliatory approach to the insurgency in Kashmir.
June 12 - Deve Gowda wins a parliamentary confidence vote with Congress party support.
June 28 - Communists join the government for the first time since independence from Britain as Deve Gowda expands cabinet.
July 3 - Government raises fuel prices, stirring a storm of criticism from communist allies and Congress.
July 6 - Deve Gowda tours rebellious Jammu and Kashmir state -- the first prime minister in a decade to do so.
September 7 - Voters in Jammu and Kashmir vote in first local polls since insurgency erupted in 1990.
September 22 - Former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao resigns as Congress president amid corruption allegations that he denies.
September 23 - Sitaram Kesri elected Congress president.
October 2 - Pro-India National Conference party wins absolute majority in Jammu and Kashmir state elections.

October 8 - The Samajwadi Party, a key socialist group in the ruling coalition, threatens to quit the government if Deve Gowda supports Congress' efforts to form a government in Uttar Pradesh with low-caste Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP).
October 11 - State assembly elections in the crucial northern province of Uttar Pradesh produce a hung assembly.
October 16 - Congress says it will review support to the government because the United Front refuses to support its Uttar Pradesh ally, the BSP.
January 1, 1997 - Congress leaders say United Front may not last full term.
January 3 - Congress chooses Kesri as its new parliamentary leader. He reiterates the party's support for the coalition.
February 12 - A Sikh-Hindu alliance of the Akali Dal party and the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) wins a landslide victory in assembly polls in northern state of Punjab.
February 28 - Government unveils market-friendly budget.
March 19 - BJP agrees with the BSP to form a government in Uttar Pradesh, posing a fresh threat to Congress.
March 30 - Congress withdraws support to the United Front.
March 31 - Congress stakes its claim to form a new government. President Shankar Dayal Sharma asks Deve Gowda to prove majority in a parliamentary confidence vote on April 11.
April 5 - Kesri lashes out at Deve Gowda, saying he would support the coalition only if it chooses a new leader. United Front says a change in leadership is out of the question.
April 9 - United Front and Congress start formal talks to resolve the political crisis.
April 10 - Congress party tells deputies to vote out Deve Gowda after talks with the United Front fail.

April 11 - BJP and its allies decide to vote against Deve Gowda. Parties agree to take up the budget during a three-day session starting on April 21. Deve Gowda loses the parliamentary vote of confidence in his 10-month-old coalition, then tenders resignation. He agrees to remain as caretaker prime minister.
April 12 - Congress says it will support the United Front in a new government if the alliance replaces Deve Gowda as leader.
April 12 - President Sharma agrees on a special parliamentary session on the budget for April 21-23.
April 13 - Deve Gowda offers to quit as United Front leader, opening the way to possible reconciliation with Congress.
April 14 - Congress says crisis can be settled in a week.
April 16 - Left-wing bloc in United Front demands that Congress withdraw its March 31 claim to form a new government.
April 17 - President Sharma meets leaders of three main political formations as United Front, Congress remain at odds.
April 18 - United Front says fresh Congress letter to President Sharma offering to withdraw its claim to form a government clears way for talks to choose new prime minister.
April 19 - United Front names departing foreign minister Inder Kumar Gujral as its leader to head the new government.
April 20 - President Sharma names Gujral prime minister after United Front and Congress set up a joint committee to try to ensure a more stable government.
April 21 - Gujral sworn in as 12th prime minister. He keeps most ministers from Deve Gowda's cabinet, but departing finance minister P. Chidambaram is not included.
